questions.question: Which statement correctly describes DynamoDB's core data model?
options: A table contains items, and each item is a collection of attributes
A table contains joins, and each join owns a partition
Every item in a table must declare the same non-key attributes
A sort key chooses the AWS Region for an item
questions.explanation: A DynamoDB table contains items, and each item contains attributes. Only the primary-key attributes are required by the table schema; other attributes can differ between items.

questions.question: A workload writes 600 items per second, each 2.2 KB, to one partition-key value. What write-unit pressure does that key create before sharding?
options: 600 WCU per second
1,000 WCU per second
1,200 WCU per second
1,800 WCU per second
questions.explanation: Each write is rounded up in 1 KB units, so a 2.2 KB item costs 3 WCU. At 600 writes per second, that key asks for 1,800 WCU per second and can exceed the per-partition design ceiling.

questions.question: Why should a DynamoDB schema begin with named access patterns?
options: DynamoDB automatically adds a JOIN for every access pattern
Keys and indexes must be shaped for the queries the application will actually issue
Access patterns determine the table's AWS account
They remove the need to test traffic distribution
questions.explanation: DynamoDB does not provide arbitrary joins and is optimized for key-based access. Listing the required reads and writes first lets the team design primary keys, sort-key ranges, and secondary indexes deliberately.

questions.question: An application must query orders by status and creation time. Which design is valid?
options: A GSI with status as partition key and creation time as sort key, accepting eventual consistency
A strongly consistent query against a GSI
A FilterExpression that makes a full table scan free
A replica used as an independent backup
questions.explanation: A GSI can provide an alternate partition and sort key, but GSI reads are eventually consistent. Its key distribution and capacity must also be reviewed because index pressure can throttle base-table writes.

questions.question: Two workers concurrently reserve the last inventory unit. What is the smallest authoritative correctness boundary?
options: An eventually consistent read followed by an unconditional update
A strongly consistent read used as a lock
A conditional update that decrements only when enough stock remains
A DynamoDB Stream consumer
questions.explanation: A conditional UpdateItem evaluates the stock invariant atomically with the mutation. A pre-read, even a strong one, does not lock the item against another writer.

questions.question: BatchWriteItem returns several UnprocessedItems. What should the client do?
options: Assume the full batch committed atomically
Retry only the unprocessed requests with bounded exponential backoff and jitter
Repeat every item immediately without a delay
Switch all reads to strong consistency
questions.explanation: BatchWriteItem is not atomic as a whole. Successfully processed items should not be replayed blindly; retry the returned UnprocessedItems with bounded backoff and preserve idempotent behavior.

questions.question: Why should a Lambda consumer of DynamoDB Streams be idempotent?
options: A failed Lambda batch can be retried and records can be processed again
Streams support strongly consistent queries
Idempotency increases a partition key's byte limit
Every stream record represents a full table backup
questions.explanation: Lambda retries failed stream batches, so duplicate processing can occur. The consumer must make repeated delivery produce the same business result rather than a duplicate charge, email, or projection update.

questions.question: What happens when DynamoDB point-in-time recovery restores a table?
options: It rewinds the existing table in place
It restores the selected recovery point into a new table
It removes the need to reapply stream and alarm settings
It guarantees that replicas did not copy an accidental write
questions.explanation: PITR restores the selected point into a new table. Operators must validate the restored data, reapply required settings that are not restored automatically, and deliberately cut traffic over.
